github.author: jerridan

identity.head: b7d91c5a0fb4306c3dbe382238118b28e85e4004
identity.description:
Release by semver tag from package.json and run the action from its own commit

A release is now the tag `v<version>` and a GitHub Release, created by a workflow from `version` in `package.json`. The hand-run procedure in the README, with its SHA pin bump and the moving `v1` tag, is gone.

## Changes

- `scripts/release-tag.sh` reads `version` from `package.json`, requires `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, refuses a ref other than `refs/heads/main` unless in dry run, and checks whether `v<version>` exists on origin. When it is absent, it runs one `gh release create` with `--target HEAD`, so GitHub creates the tag and the release together. No `git tag`, no `git push`, no tagger identity, and a tag never moves. When the tag exists, it prints one line and exits 0.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs that script on every push to `main` and on a manual dispatch with a `dry_run` input. Permissions are `contents: write` only, the checkout keeps no credentials, and a concurrency group serialises runs.
- `scripts/check-version-bump.sh` fails a pull request that changes `src/`, `prompts/`, `action.yml` or `review.yml` without raising the version, by semver order, in `package.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` together. The `checks` job of `ci.yml` runs it on pull requests.
- `.github/workflows/review.yml` runs the action from a fresh checkout of this repo at `job.workflow_sha`, the commit of the workflow file itself, so the action and the workflow always come from one commit and no pin inside the repo needs a bump. The workspace rule relaxes from "never build in the workspace" to "never build the pull request's own files", with two guards: a step deletes anything the pull request placed at `.pr-review-action` and the workspace `node_modules`, and the checkout sets `persist-credentials: false`. The reviewers read a worktree built from git objects, so they never see the directory.
- `.github/actionlint.yaml` ignores one message for `review.yml`: actionlint 1.7.12 does not yet know `job.workflow_sha`, which the GitHub contexts reference documents.
- `pr-review.yml` of this repo calls `review.yml@main`. `action.yml` gets Marketplace branding. The README, the design doc and CLAUDE.md describe the new flow, and a consumer references `@v<version>`.
- The three version fields move from 0.1.0 to 0.2.0, so the merge of this pull request creates `v0.2.0`.

## After the merge

- `release.yml` tags `v0.2.0` at the merge commit and creates the release. Watch the first run.
- Delete the old tag by hand, once: `git push origin --delete v1`. Nothing references it after this change.
- To list the action on the Marketplace, open the release and publish it. That click is manual.

## Tests

The red commit 83e6d61 adds `test/release-scripts.test.ts` alone, and all fourteen tests fail there because the script does not exist. The tests run both scripts in a temporary git repository with a bare remote and a stateful `gh` stub that creates the tag on `release create`, the way GitHub does. They cover the release, the idempotent second run, both dry-run selectors, the ref and token refusals, malformed versions, a remote read failure, and every row of the version-check table including a lowered version. The packaging tests assert the release workflow's shape, the local action with its two guard steps, the branding, and that the plugin version equals the package version.

`npm test` (1105 pass), `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` and `actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml` all pass. `scripts/check-version-bump.sh` exits 0 on this branch.

## Charter

Goal: replace the hand-run release procedure with a release driven by `version` in `package.json`, and make the reusable workflow run the action from its own commit so the SHA pin inside the repo goes away. The principal decided: semver tags with no moving `v1`; the version bump lives in the feature pull request; this repo calls `review.yml@main`; one version across `package.json` and both plugin manifests, enforced in CI; Marketplace publishing stays manual; the workspace rule relaxes to "never build the pull request's own files" with the guards above.

## Decisions

- Path: the change path. Not the light path: six items across workflows, scripts, tests and docs, with two preference questions open.
- Preference answers: `@main` for this repo's own workflow; one version across the three files. Neither recorded as a CLAUDE.md rule; the README states both.
- Spec critic round 1 (3 critical, 9 concern, 3 nit): the "logic in a script" and "values through env" constraints were missing; `uses: ./` conflicted with the workspace security rule and its tests; the release script's credentials and tagger identity were unspecified. All fixed. The security conflict went to the principal, who chose to relax the rule with the guards.
- Spec critic round 2 (0 critical, 4 concern, 6 nit): Node module resolution could walk up to the workspace `node_modules`, so the guard step deletes it; the version check takes two positional SHAs and reads the base version at the base SHA; two greps added to the docs acceptance. All folded in.
- Shape: simple path, one package, band deep, because the package changes a security boundary and the criterion took interpretation.
- actionlint 1.7.12 rejects `job.workflow_sha`; one scoped ignore in `.github/actionlint.yaml` with a comment that names the cause.

triage.summary: The change introduces a tag-based release process. A new release workflow and script create v<version> releases from package.json, and a CI check requires a version bump when shipped files change. The reusable review workflow now checks out its own repo at job.workflow_sha and runs the action from there, and action.yml copies itself to the runner temp directory before it installs, builds and runs. Docs and tests are updated, and versions go to 0.2.0.
